_source: Deterministic parse of raw Telair PBX CSV exports (ExportCallRecords, InboundCalls_Detailed, CallQueue_Detailed per queue) via scripts/parse_call_logs.py, built directly from raw-source data from the start. Core figures close to Daily Operations Report - 13th October 2026.pdf but with a handful of small, verbatim-recorded gaps this date — see _summaryVsGrandTotalNote, _staffCountNote, _patientServiceKpiNote and _outboundDurationNote. Two queue-level source rows (one each in the Appointments and General Enquiries CallQueue_Detailed CSVs) appeared as an exact duplicate CallGUID in the raw export; the parser's own per-queue counts still matched the PDF's own queue breakdown exactly, so this looks like deduplicated correctly rather than double-counted, but is noted here for transparency.
_summaryVsGrandTotalNote: Three numbers disagree by small amounts this date: the PDF's own cover prints 247 total/222 accepted/25 missed; this file's queue-level grandTotal (from the four named queues) sums to 221 accepted/25 missed (246 total) — 1 short of the PDF's own cover, a pre-existing inconsistency in the PDF's own numbers (its cover total doesn't equal its own queue breakdown sum), not introduced here; and this file's own summary (from the deduplicated InboundCalls_Detailed file) reads 248 total/223 accepted — 1 OVER the PDF's cover. The extra accepted call traces to a single agent, Rebecca Quinn, whose own raw tally is 68 calls/151 min versus the PDF's own printed 67 calls/145 min (see _staffCountNote) — all three figures recorded verbatim rather than reconciled to agree.
_tenDayTrendNote: accepted/missed/answerRatePct/overallAvgWaitSec all chain-matched 2026-10-12's own committed trend exactly at positions 0-8; position 9 is this date's own raw-CSV-derived figure (223 accepted, 25 missed, 90% answer rate, 44 sec overall average wait).
_queuesNote: accepted/missed for all four queues chain-match 2026-10-12's own committed data exactly at positions 0-8, and all three non-zero queues' accepted/missed at position 9 match the PDF's own queue breakdown exactly (Appointments 143/7, General Enquiries 77/18, Canberra Vasectomy 1/0). avgWaitSec at position 9 matches the PDF's own per-queue 10-day charts exactly for all three (Appointments 40 sec, General Enquiries 53 sec, Canberra Vasectomy 56 sec).
_patientServiceKpiNote: longestCallDurationSec/longestCallAt/longestCallAgent and longestWaitingTimeSec/longestWaitingAt all match the PDF's own Patient Service KPI panel exactly (553 sec at 4:02 PM by Lucinda Gonzalez; 402 sec at 11:26 AM). avgCallHandlingSec computes to 151 sec here versus the PDF's own printed 150 sec — a 1-second rounding difference on the averaging method, recorded verbatim rather than adjusted.
_staffCountNote: 11 of inboundByStaff's 12 names match the PDF's own printed Inbound Calls - All Staff table exactly on both calls and duration. The exception is Rebecca Quinn, whose raw tally here is 68 calls/151 min versus the PDF's own printed 67 calls/145 min — the single extra accepted call behind the summary-vs-grandTotal gap above (see _summaryVsGrandTotalNote), recorded verbatim rather than trimmed to match the PDF.
_outboundDurationNote: outboundByStaff's own call counts match the PDF's own 13-name outbound staff table exactly for every name (22/12/10/10/9/8/6/4/4/4/3/2/1, summing to the confirmed 95-call total, which also matches this file's own summary.totalOutbound and the PDF's own 'Total Outbound Calls = 95 Calls' header exactly — no reception-scope gap this date, unlike 2026-10-12). Several per-agent durationMins values differ from the PDF's own printed minutes by 1-3 (e.g. Ambrosie Brassil 30 here vs 33 printed), while Rebecca Quinn/Holly Archer/Kiara Pfeffer/Kate Chin match exactly — consistent with each source rounding individual call durations to the nearest minute before summing in a slightly different way, not a data error; recorded verbatim rather than adjusted to match.
